office: the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security

routes.label: at a civil registration office of the Ministry

cards.for: anyone, a first card or a renewal

note: The Ministry's chief registrar, at an e-ID awareness campaign in Gobabis (The Namibian, 29 July 2026): first-time applicants, those renewing expired cards and those amending their records receive the new electronic identity card free; only a duplicate for a lost or damaged card carries the prescribed replacement fee (not modelled). The card's term, the age at which it is due and the time weren't read.

sources.title: The Namibian, Ministry of home affairs clarifies e-ID costs (29 July 2026)
sources.said: The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security has clarified that Namibians applying for the new electronic identity (e-ID) card will not be required to pay, with fees only applicable under limited circumstances such as replacing recently issued lost or damaged cards. ... said first-time applicants, those renewing expired identity cards and applicants making amendments to their identity records would receive the new e-ID
